review_points.topic: Fixed name backgrounds and hit rectangles
review_points.finding: The same NAME_SIGNS entry supplies the uploaded canvas size, GeoJSON sign identifier and layout width/height. Five original-size canvases at pixelRatio=2 produce 84x34, 120x34, 176x34, 176x48 and 176x62 CSS-pixel cards. Both name and numbered layers use icon-text-fit:none, so native text fitting no longer changes the background bounds after layout. hitTestBeaconLabels still uses those layout bounds in reverse draw order.

All 70 catalogue names keep their original text. The current longest weighted title is 21.85 units and selects the two-line 176x48 background; no current name reaches the three-line maximum. Text remains max-width12 em and line-height1.17 for full names. This bounds review does not certify exact glyph appearance; final browser images are required.

longest_current_title.name: 北大街222号民居（2022年鹤龙美术馆使用状态）

review_points.finding: projectBeaconAnchor calls the actual transform.locationToScreenPoint with an elevation provider returning zero. This matches the GeoJSON ground anchor rather than Map.project’s elevated centre plane. Records retain original geographic point geometry; only layout offsets are moved in CSS pixels. The helper falls back to map.project when a transform implementation is absent.

For an elevated transform, ground-valid label slots use screenPointToMercatorCoordinateAtZ(slot,-elevation); at zero elevation the former map.unproject branch remains. Slots above the ground horizon are not unprojected. This keeps visible leader endpoints on the same zero-altitude plane as symbol anchors.
review_points.status: consistent with reviewed actual-vendor round-trip test

review_points.finding: For native positive anchor depth W, the shader factor r=clamp(0.5+0.5*C/W,0,4) is inverted. Uploaded icon-size becomes 1/r and text-size12/r for each on-screen ID. Icon offsets retain desired CSS displacement d, and text offsets d/12 em. Consequently icon displacement d*(1/r)*r=d, text displacement (d/12)*(12/r)*r=d, and both drawn bounds equal the original layout rectangles. The formula uses ground-relative world displacement, bearing, pitch and centre elevation; reviewed vendor evidence compares against homogeneous W from _pixelMatrix3D independently.
review_points.status: algebraically consistent for the reviewed visible/front-of-camera anchors

review_points.finding: With pitch0 and elevation0, W=C, so r=1; sizeExpression emits the former constants icon-size1 and text-size12. Number canvas remains48x40 at pixelRatio2, yielding24x20. Existing two-pixel then zero-pixel compact-grid fallback and screen-rectangle hit logic are retained. No new candidate IDs, coordinate records, or catalogue assets are changed.
review_points.status: former flat numbering contract retained by inspection

review_points.finding: There remain four layers (leader, original lamp, full-name card, numbered card) and the same70 model IDs. Viewport filters remain on cards only. scope_limits: Earlier ten-group and compact-capacity reports keep their original source bindings; they are not relabeled as full reruns on this source.
This review did not open Chrome, run WebGL, repeat the24 beacon tests, or rerun unrelated city/clipping/shader suites.

Perspective and inverse conclusions concern the shipped Mercator, zero-ground, visible/front-of-camera path exercised by the cited tests. Final glyph legibility, pixel alignment and mouse/touch behavior are verified by the separate final browser QA.
